**Grade Certification Process for TTU K-12**

**Grade Certification Before End of Term**

For Texas Tech K-12, grades are typically certified and recorded after the completion of a course. Here are the key points regarding grade certification:

- **Assignment Grading**: Teachers have up to two business days to grade assignments once they are received.

- **Course Completion**: Grades are officially recorded and certified once a course is completed. This means that a final grade is posted to the student's account and can be viewed in the Focus portal.

- **Grade Reports**: Once grades are posted, students or their school counselors can download or request a hard copy of the grade report.

If you need a grade certified before the end of the term for a specific reason, it would be best to contact Texas Tech K-12 directly to discuss your situation. You can reach them at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Attendance/Progress Requirements for students in the Texas Tech K-12 Tuition-Free Program

The following attendance requirement applies to all full-time students who are Texas residents and who are enrolled in the tuition-free program, unless a specific exemption has been granted by a school administrator.

Step 1: In your all-online program, “attendance” will be defined as progress within each semester course.

Step 2: You will have six months (180 days from the date of enrollment) to complete each semester course.

Step 3: You must maintain enrollment in a minimum of four semester courses.

Step 4: You must complete a minimum of 5% of course assignments in every seven-day period. For example, if your course has 20 assignments, you need to complete a minimum of one per week. If your course has 60 assignments, you must average a minimum of three per week.

Q: How does this impact admissions to universities?

A: In high performing school districts like TTU K-12, students who rank outside the top 10% would normally rank very high at other districts. This can hurt our students in college admissions. If a student has been given a rank by a high school, for example, the 40th percentile, many universities will use that rank as a shortcut to evaluate the student and say that student falls in the top 40% of all applicants to the university. However, if the student does not have a high school rank, the university will evaluate the student's record and assign them a rank relative to other applicants. When compared to other college applicants, our students tend to be more qualified than those who graduate with a similar ranking at other high schools. According to other Texas districts, schools saw a 38% increase in acceptance to the University of Texas and a 49% increase to Texas A&M after eliminating class rank.

Student Conduct and Academic Integrity

Texas Tech K-12 fosters a spirit of complete honesty and a high standard of integrity. An attempt to present any work you have not honestly performed as your own is regarded by Texas Tech K-12 as a serious offense leading to serious consequences.

As a part of Texas Tech University, the Texas Tech K-12 student conduct policy aligns with the university’s student policy regarding academic integrity:

“Academic dishonesty includes, but is not limited to, cheating, plagiarism, collusion, falsifying academic records, misrepresenting facts, and any act designed to give an unfair academic advantage to the student (such as, but not limited to, submission of essentially the same written assignment for two courses).”

For a full description of each of the examples above, please read Section I, Part B.1, Academic Dishonesty in the TTU Student Conduct Policy (opens in new tab).

When may I enroll?

Texas Tech K-12 does not operate on a semester basis; therefore, courses are asynchronous. Open enrollment allows you to enroll in any course, at any time, and work at your own pace. If you are enrolled in another district, obtain approval from your school counselor before enrolling in a course to ensure credit upon successful completion.

My child has an Individualized Education Program (or 504 plan). May he/she enroll in your school?

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

Nevertheless, Texas Tech K-12 strives to offer exceptional education programs that meet the needs of students with disabilities. To qualify, the student's Individual Education Plan (IEP) needs to indicate that the Texas Tech K-12 online program is the appropriate instructional setting for the student and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

The student’s admission, review, and dismissal (ARD) committee has the responsibility of determining whether or not an electronic (online) course/program will meet the needs of a student with a disability. The committee will also take into account the nature of the asynchronous program and what services can be implemented online. It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. The Admission Review Dismissal committee will make an informed decision about an online program and the educational appropriateness of this academic setting for a student and his or her particular academic needs.

Step 3: Entrance exams help assess academic and English proficiency before admission.

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exams excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exams excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

Additional information may be found at State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness (STAAR Testing) (opens in new tab).

Texas law (HB 4545 /1416) states that any student who did not pass a State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness (STAAR) exam the previous year is REQUIRED to receive 15-30 hours of additional remedial instruction in that content area per year. Minimum Lesson/Unit Completion Requirements

Students demonstrate attendance in Texas Tech K-12 online school by regularly completing assignments. Attendance is directly tied to what the student accomplishes and/or produces over a given period. The assignments completed are the evidence that a student has been in attendance, and if no work is produced, then a student is not considered to be in attendance.

Unless specifically stated otherwise, attendance is required a minimum of 3 days per week. A student must complete at least 5% of course assignments in a seven-day period and in every subsequent seven-day period until the course is completed.

Course completion is required to earn course credit. No partial course credit will be granted. Course credit is earned when the student has successfully demonstrated mastery of the Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills for the course.

Students have six months from the date of enrollment to complete each course. To remain in the program, students must be concurrently enrolled in a minimum of four courses.

Earning dual credit in high school offers several benefits. Firstly, it allows students to get a head start on their college education by earning college credits while still in high school. Required Attendance at Texas Tech K-12

The following attendance requirement applies to all full-time students who are Texas residents and who are enrolled in the tuition-free program, unless a specific exemption has been granted by a school administrator.

WHAT HAPPENS IF I CANNOT BE THERE TO TEST?

If you are ill or have an emergency, please contact your testing coordinator immediately. To ensure that you remain on schedule to graduate, participation in and successful completion of both State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness and State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness/End Of Course is necessary and is a condition of your enrollment with Texas Tech K-12. Failure to test will result in removal from the tuition-free program per our attendance policy.

Identification Cards and Verification of Enrollment (VOE)

As a full-time student, you are eligible to receive a Texas Tech K-12 student identification card and Verification of Attendance (VOE).

Verification of Attendance

If you are a full-time student who wishes to receive a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) for any purpose, including a driver’s permit, Social Security benefits or child support, avoiding truancy in your local district, or legal documentation of enrollment in a Texas Tech K-12 full-time program, you MUST meet the full-time student eligibility requirements as outlined above.

You may request a Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) Verification of Enrollment and Attendance Form or an official letter verifying enrollment and attendance from your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. Texas Tech K-12 administration may deny verification of enrollment and attendance to any student who has not maintained adequate progress to stay on grade level. Request a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance by emailing a request to your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. The advisor will require at least two working days for progress review.

If you are denied a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance, your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor will work with you to outline a progress intervention plan to meet the requirements necessary to receive a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance in the future.

Minimum Lesson/Unit Completion Requirements

Students demonstrate attendance in Texas Tech K-12 online school by regularly completing assignments. Attendance is directly tied to what the student accomplishes and/or produces over a given period. The assignments completed are the evidence that a student has been in attendance, and if no work is produced, then a student is not considered to be in attendance.

Unless specifically stated otherwise, attendance is required a minimum of 3 days per week. A student must complete at least 5% of course assignments in a seven-day period and in every subsequent seven-day period until the course is completed.

Course completion is required to earn course credit. No partial course credit will be granted. Course credit is earned when the student has successfully demonstrated mastery of the Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills for the course.

Students have six months from the date of enrollment to complete each course. To remain in the program, students must be concurrently enrolled in a minimum of four courses.

Failure to meet minimum progress requirements may cause Texas Tech K-12 to implement truancy processes and may result in your removal from the program.

Participation in mandatory state testing is a condition of enrollment in our tuition free program and is a requirement from the Texas Education Agency for graduation under the Foundation High School program. Students who do not participate in state testing will be moved to the tuition paid program.

**Admission Process for Texas Tech K-12**

1. **Program Selection:**
   - Decide between the Tuition-Free Program (for Texas residents only) and the Full-Time Tuition-Based Program (for students outside Texas or those seeking more flexibility).

2. **Eligibility Requirements:**
   - **Tuition-Free Program:**
     - Must be a Texas resident under the age of 25.
     - Provide proof of residency and a copy of your birth certificate.
     - Enroll in at least four semester courses and maintain satisfactory progress.
   - **Tuition-Based Program:**
     - Available to students outside Texas or those who prefer fewer restrictions.

3. **Application Steps:**
   - Complete the Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form.
   - Pay the non-refundable admission fee:
     - $200 for domestic students.
     - $250 for international students (includes a $50 entrance exam fee).

4. **Enrollment Process:**
   - For the Tuition-Free Program, enrollment is limited and uses a lottery system each semester.
   - For the Tuition-Based Program, enrollment is open and flexible.

5. **Payment and Fees:**
   - Upon enrollment, payment is due. Texas Tech K-12 does not offer payment plans.
   - Students are responsible for purchasing their own books and materials.

For more detailed information or specific inquiries, you can contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

My Child has an Individualized Education Program (IEP) or 504 plan. May he/she enroll in your school?

Texas Tech K-12’s curriculum is developed to meet the standards of the State of Texas and the Texas Education Agency. Accommodations will be implemented based on the student’s current Individual Education Plan (IEP) or 504 documentation. The student’s IEP or 504 should reflect that Texas Tech K-12 is an appropriate placement and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

A student should obtain information regarding available disability accommodations before enrolling in a course or CBE. Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exams excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course exams to meet graduation requirements.

1. **Visit the Texas Tech K-12 Website:**
   - Access the enrollment forms and program details on the Texas Tech K-12 website.

2. **Select the Program:**
   - Choose the appropriate program, such as the Supplemental Individual Student (Part-Time) or Full-Time Tuition-Based Program, depending on your needs.

3. **Complete the Enrollment Form:**
   - Use the Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form to apply for enrollment. Specify the AP course you wish to take.

4. **Submit Required Documents:**
   - Provide necessary documentation, such as proof of residency or previous academic records, if applicable.

5. **Pay the Fees:**
   - Pay the required admission and course fees. For international students, the course fee is $450.00 per course.

6. **Access Course Materials:**
   - Once enrolled, you will receive access to course materials and instructions on how to begin your course.

For more detailed information or specific inquiries, you can contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Online School vs. Homeschooling**

When deciding between online school and homeschooling, consider the following factors:

**Online School (e.g., Texas Tech K-12):**
- **Structured Curriculum:** Provides a structured curriculum with set courses and materials.
- **Accreditation:** Offers accredited programs that can be beneficial for college applications.
- **Flexibility:** Allows students to learn at their own pace within a structured framework.
- **Support Services:** Access to teachers and support staff for guidance and assistance.

**Homeschooling:**
- **Customization:** Allows for a fully customized curriculum tailored to the student's interests and learning style.
- **Parental Control:** Parents have full control over the educational content and pace.
- **Flexibility:** Offers complete flexibility in scheduling and learning methods.
- **Resource Intensive:** Requires parents to source or create educational materials and resources.

**Considerations:**
- **Learning Style:** Consider your child's learning style and whether they thrive in a structured or flexible environment.
- **Parental Involvement:** Assess the level of involvement you can commit to as a parent in either setting.
- **Goals:** Determine your educational goals, such as college preparation or skill development.

Both options have their advantages and challenges, and the best choice depends on your specific circumstances and educational goals. If you have more questions or need further details about Texas Tech K-12, feel free to ask!

Supplemental Program Information

Anyone looking to supplement their current school curriculum or home school curriculum can enroll in Texas Tech K-12.  Our Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) is designed to allow students in elementary, middle and high school that allows students to work at their own pace. We have students who must do their work at home for various reasons, such as travel "outside" of the U.S. for extended amounts of time, have health issues, are actors, entertainers, and athletes who cannot fit the traditional schooling into their schedule. We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. Each course has lessons, which are like chapters, and a final exam. The final exam will be proctored online by an online proctoring service.

Is this school a good fit for a student with special needs?

This is the parent’s decision.  Of course, you know your child best and you are the best person to determine the environment in which your child will experience the most success.

Many students with special needs do very well in our online program. Some of these needs that are readily accommodated include:  use of a screen reader, need larger font, need highlighting or color change functionality, need a learning environment free from distractions, need extended time on exams, have social anxiety, have medical concerns. Our online courses are fully accessible and meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0 federal web compliance requirements.

Texas Tech K-12 may not be the most appropriate instructional setting and the least restrictive environment for your child (see above), as required by federal law.

Texas Tech K-12 is a statewide online school district and does not have a physical campus nor a geographic service district. We serve full-time students from across the entire state of Texas.

We have special education personnel to ensure and monitor appropriate accommodations identified in the Individualized Education Program or 504 plan. We closely monitor the academic progress of all students and will provide appropriate interventions and services as identified.

Again, as the parent, you will need to make an individualized analysis. We are happy to share more information about the nature of our coursework if that would be helpful in your decision-making process.

What does an "asynchronous" online program mean?

Step 1: It means that all instruction takes place at your student's own timing and pace. The student will not receive instruction via Zoom or another virtual platform at a predetermined time and date.

Step 2: Some students with special needs found that a synchronous online program (one-on-one with a teacher) worked well with them during the pandemic. Our program is asynchronous (instruction is self-paced and not time-driven, so it is not one-on-one with a teacher). As a result, this instructional environment may not be the most appropriate instructional setting for your child.

Step 3: Our teachers host office hours that allow for students to join them. Office hours are posted inside the course.

As a result, this instructional environment may not be the most appropriate instructional setting for your child.

Our teachers do offer office hours which allow for students to meet with them. Dates and times of teacher office hours are posted in each course.

Single Diploma

The Single Diploma track is for students who want to complete all their high school education through Texas Tech K-12 and earn a Texas high school diploma.

Step 1: Students use Texas Tech K-12 curriculum entirely through online courses.

Step 2: This track is best for students with strong English skills due to the rigorous demands of reading, writing, and speaking in English.

Step 3: Ideal for: Students wanting a fully online education with a Texas high school diploma.

About Students with Disabilities

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

Nevertheless, Texas Tech K-12 strives to offer exceptional education programs that meet the needs of students with disabilities. To qualify, the student's Individual Education Plan (IEP) needs to indicate that the Texas Tech K-12 online program is the appropriate instructional setting for the student and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

The student’s admission, review, and dismissal (ARD) committee has the responsibility of determining whether or not an electronic (online) course/program will meet the needs of a student with a disability. The committee will also take into account the nature of the asynchronous program and what services can be implemented online. It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. The ARD committee will make an informed decision about an online program and the educational appropriateness of this academic setting for a student and his or her particular academic needs.

Compulsory Attendance

Good attendance is critical for academic success. This is true in both traditional and online schools. In an online school environment, establishing a consistent routine every day yields the maximum academic benefit.

In 2015, the Texas legislature removed the criminal offense of failure to attend school from the Texas Education Code. Instead, districts are required to address student truancy by implementing prevention measures, identifying circumstances contributing to a student's unexcused absences, and taking specific actions. Although truancy is no longer a criminal offense, districts may still refer a student to truancy court as an action of last resort.

How is attendance tracked in an online school?

Step 1: Attendance is based on progress in your child’s courses.

Step 2: Your child must complete 5% of each course's assignments each week. For example, if a course has 20 assignments, at least one should be completed each week.

Step 3: Courses must be completed within the designated tuition free program semester timeline.

Step 4: Students must stay enrolled in at least four courses.

How do I apply:

Step 1: New students enter a lottery every six months (fall for the new school year and January for mid-year transfers).

Step 2: If not selected, you’ll be placed on a waitlist and notified if a spot opens.

Conduct

You are responsible for your personal conduct and behavior. A distance education course, whether online or in print, carries the same expectations as a course in a traditional classroom. The teacher monitors and evaluates student conduct and behavior, and you will be held accountable for your words and actions.

Behavior or language not appropriate for a traditional classroom is likewise not appropriate in a Texas Tech K-12 course. This includes, but is not limited to, the use of profanity and the refusal to complete assignments. Behaving in this manner may result in being dropped from your course(s). By enrolling in a course or CBE, you have entered into an agreement with Texas Tech K-12 to refrain from the use of profanity in both written and oral communication and to behave in an appropriate and respectful manner at all times.

For further information regarding student conduct in a Texas Tech K-12 course, please read the Texas Tech K-12 Policies

Attendance/Progress Requirements for students in the Texas Tech K-12 Tuition-Free Program

The following attendance requirement applies to all full-time students who are Texas residents and who are enrolled in the tuition-free program, unless a specific exemption has been granted by a school administrator.

Step 1: In your all-online program, “attendance” will be defined as progress within each semester course.

Step 2: You will have six months (180 days from the date of enrollment) to complete each semester course.

Step 3: You must maintain enrollment in a minimum of four semester courses.

Step 4: You must complete a minimum of 5% of course assignments in every seven-day period. For example, if your course has 20 assignments, you need to complete a minimum of one per week. If your course has 60 assignments, you must average a minimum of three per week.

Step 5: Please note:

Step 6: Completing the minimum number of assignments does not guarantee you will complete within the 6-month time frame.

Step 7: Completing the minimum number of assignments and courses may not maintain your appropriate grade level or anticipated graduation date.

Step 8: If your progress is adequate, your parent may request “vacation” days. These must be requested and approved in advance.

What does an "Asynchronous" online program mean?

Step 1: This means students complete lessons on their own time and pace, without live virtual classes. It may not be suitable for all students, especially those who need more direct teacher interaction.

Where do I go to enroll online?

Students that are interested in enrolling should select the course from the course catalog (opens in new tab). Once you have selected your course, please click "enroll now" which will take you to the intake form to complete the enrollment process. Prior to enrolling, please coordinate with your local school counselor concerning the local school policies and other requirements.

Graduation Requirements for Texas Tech High School Students

As a student enrolled in Texas Tech High School, you have several options for earning a high school diploma, depending on the date of your enrollment in ninth grade:

Step 1: Students enrolled in ninth grade before the 2014-15 school year must complete the Recommended High School Program (RHSP) or the Minimum High School Program (MHSP) and meet state testing requirements for your graduation plan. In some cases, you may be permitted to graduate on the Foundation Graduation Plan or the Foundation with Endorsement Graduation Plan and earn a Distinguished Level of Achievement.

Step 2: Students enrolled in ninth grade during or after the 2014-15 school year must complete the Foundation Graduation Plan plus Endorsement.

Step 3: For complete information regarding Texas graduation requirements, refer to the graduation section of the TEA website (opens in new tab).

For Students

Note: All courses and most of our Credit by Exams will utilize an online proctoring service called Proctorio. Pathway to Success - Earn Credits Before Graduation

Earning dual credit in high school offers several benefits, especially through online dual credit courses like those offered by Texas Tech K-12. Students can complete their initial two years of undergraduate studies at Texas Tech K-12 before transitioning to Texas Tech for their final two years after high school graduation. This pathway provides a seamless transition to higher education and allows students to begin their college journey early.

Minimum Lesson/Unit Completion Requirements

Students demonstrate attendance in Texas Tech K-12 online school by regularly completing assignments. Attendance is directly tied to what the student accomplishes and/or produces over a given period. The assignments completed are the evidence that a student has been in attendance, and if no work is produced, then a student is not considered to be in attendance.

Unless specifically stated otherwise, attendance is required a minimum of 3 days per week. A student must complete at least 5% of course assignments in a seven-day period and in every subsequent seven-day period until the course is completed.

All course grades while you are enrolled in Texas Tech K-12 will be recorded on your transcript and used in computing your final Grade Point Average. However, you may replace a failing grade you received on a Texas Tech K-12 course or Credit By Exam by repeating the course or Credit By Exam.

As an assistant, I don't have personal opinions, but I can provide you with information to help you make an informed decision between online school and homeschooling:

**Online School (e.g., Texas Tech K-12):**
- **Structured Curriculum:** Offers a structured and accredited curriculum, which can be beneficial for college applications.
- **Flexibility:** Allows students to learn at their own pace within a structured framework.
- **Support Services:** Provides access to teachers and support staff for guidance and assistance.
- **Accessibility:** Meets Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, accommodating various learning needs.

**Homeschooling:**
- **Customization:** Allows for a fully customized curriculum tailored to the student's interests and learning style.
- **Parental Control:** Parents have full control over the educational content and pace.
- **Flexibility:** Offers complete flexibility in scheduling and learning methods.
- **Resource Intensive:** Requires parents to source or create educational materials and resources.

**Considerations:**
- **Learning Style:** Consider your child's learning style and whether they thrive in a structured or flexible environment.
- **Parental Involvement:** Assess the level of involvement you can commit to as a parent in either setting.
- **Goals:** Determine your educational goals, such as college preparation or skill development.

Both options have their advantages and challenges, and the best choice depends on your specific circumstances and educational goals. If you have more questions or need further details about Texas Tech K-12, feel free to ask!

The following attendance requirement applies to all full-time students who are Texas residents and who are enrolled in the tuition-free program, unless a specific exemption has been granted by a school administrator.

Not all incoming students are required to take the Texas Success Initiative Assessment. In fact, there are several ways to earn an exemption from the Texas Success Initiative Assessment, which allows a student to enroll in any entry-level college course without restrictions.

Meeting one of the following criteria may qualify a student for a Texas Success Initiative exemption.

Step 1: Scored a 23 or higher on the ACT composite and a minimum of 19 on both English and Math (Note: for ACT administered PRIOR to February 15, 2023; scores may not be older than 5 years at the time of exemption).

Step 2: For ACT administered AFTER February 15, 2023, a combined score of 40 for English and Reading, and a score of 22 for Math.

Step 3: A SAT score of 480 of the Evidence-Based Reading and Writing (EBRW) and 530 on Math. Scores must be issued within 5 years at time of exemption.

Step 4: A STAAR minimum score on English III Reading of 2000, English III Writing of 2000, and Algebra II of 4000.

Step 5: Students transferring from other institutions having satisfactorily completed college-level coursework.

What are the benefits of earning dual credit in high school?

Earning dual credit in high school offers several benefits. Firstly, it allows students to get a head start on their college education by earning college credits while still in high school. This can lead to a more efficient and cost-effective path to obtaining a college degree. Additionally, dual credit courses provide students with exposure to the rigor and expectations of college-level coursework, helping them develop essential academic skills and prepare for the challenges of higher education. Moreover, successfully completing dual credit courses can enhance students' college applications and demonstrate their readiness for post-secondary education. Overall, dual credit offers a valuable opportunity for high school students to accelerate their academic progress and position themselves for future success.

Texas Tech K-12 high school students can start taking Texas Tech College Preparatory Academy dual credit courses as ninth graders.

What does dual credit mean in high school?

Dual credit in high school refers to courses that allow students to earn both high school and college credit simultaneously. These courses are typically offered through partnerships between high schools and colleges or universities, enabling students to get a head start on their college education while still in high school.

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exams excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course exams to meet graduation requirements.
